**Finding submitted: compliant** — no redline, no comment.

I re-checked and there is nothing to repair. The verifier's own commentary confirms the classification, the direction of analysis, and the treatment of both examination-type provisions; it also confirms the single failed check is a heuristic false signal. Re-submitting the finding unchanged in substance is therefore the correct response.

Summary of the position:

- **No Vendor audit right exists.** Section 3 runs (a)–(g) as use covenants only; Section 20 covers just time-of-essence and notices; sweeps for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "monitor", "premises", "remote" and "records" return nothing binding us.
- **Section 16 escrow** examination runs *in our favour*; **Section 17(b)** is a post-termination self-certification with no Garman entry, inspection or system access. Neither engages this rule.
- **Result:** better than preferred on frequency, notice, cost allocation and system access. No edit is warranted.

One point worth flagging for the record, since it bears on how this result should be read: the "audit frequency limited" check cannot pass on this document, because there is no audit clause for it to constrain. Further re-submissions will not change that. The only way to clear the check would be to insert audit machinery — a frequency cap, notice period and cost allocation — which would hand Garman an inspection right it does not currently have. That would be a directionally wrong edit against our own client and I have not made it. If the check needs to be satisfied for pipeline reasons, it should be marked not-applicable at the rule level rather than resolved by drafting.
